ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: High macro-level contrast ratio; approximately 70% of the visible surface consists of high-intensity white pixels in the central regions, bordered by 30% low-intensity black pixels at the margins and notch.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Large contiguous white geometric regions occupy the center of both lobes. Low-intensity black pixel streaks and mottling radiate from the median notch into the high-intensity field. Solid black pigmentation forms a continuous band along the lateral and leading edges.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped central depression with a sharp vertex. The notch depth is approximately 15% of the visible vertical lobe height.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Irregular serration across the entire trailing edge. The right lobe (image right) shows higher-amplitude pixel variations and sharper peaks compared to the left lobe, which exhibits a more consistent but still jagged topography.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Convex curvature on the lateral edges. The left lobe (image left) terminates in a rounded, inward-curving tip, while the right lobe tip appears more tapered and laterally extended.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Distinct cluster of 6-10 roughly circular, high-contrast white and grey pixel clusters localized on the distal tip of the left lobe (image left).
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Multiple dark, unaligned linear pixel disruptions are visible; specifically, three near-vertical rake marks on the lower-left lobe and one prominent diagonal scratch on the upper-central left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: A significant irregular notch-like indentation is present on the trailing edge of the right lobe, distinct from the natural serration pattern.
other_distinctive_markers: A series of high-contrast black 'brush-stroke' patterns radiating upward from the peduncle attachment point into the white ventral field.
